walkthroughs.body_html:
Sources of Wisdom & Authority — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sources of Wisdom & Authority brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sources of Wisdom & Authority.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: For Catholics, which authority officially interprets scripture and tradition?
options: The Magisterium — the Pope and bishops
Each individual believer alone
The local government
University professors

mcqs.q: How do Muslims regard the Qur'an?
options: As the direct word of Allah revealed to Muhammad
As a biography of Muhammad written centuries later
As a translation of the Torah
As a code of laws written by imams
The first five books of the Hebrew Bible
A commentary on the Talmud
A Jewish prayer book
A history of the rabbis

mcqs.q: In religious ethics, conscience is often described as what?
options: An inner, God-given sense of right and wrong
A legal ruling issued by a court
A tax paid to the church
A pilgrimage undertaken once in a lifetime

mcqs.q: Do all Christians read the Bible literally?
options: No — some Christians read it literally as the exact word of God, while liberal Christians treat parts as symbolic or shaped by human authors; interpretation varies widely.
Christians are forbidden from reading the Bible without a priest present.
Conscience is a written document kept by each church.
Every Christian believes every word of the Bible is literally true.

mcqs.q: Do Muslims believe Muhammad wrote the Qur'an?
options: Muhammad composed the Qur'an himself as a record of his own teachings.
Christians are forbidden from reading the Bible without a priest present.
The Qur'an was originally written in Latin and later translated into Arabic.
No — Muslims believe the Qur'an is the literal word of Allah revealed to Muhammad through the angel Jibril; Muhammad is the messenger, not the author.

mcqs.q: Is conscience always a reliable source of authority for believers?
options: Religious believers think any gut feeling counts as the voice of God.
Conscience is a written document kept by each church.
Christians are forbidden from reading the Bible without a priest present.
Many traditions teach conscience must be informed by scripture and church teaching first; Catholics, for example, must educate their conscience before following it.

Third section: the Writings, including Psalms
